abstract: Invasive lobular breast carcinoma (ILC) is defined by loss of the adhesion protein E-cadherin. Using a cancer histology-focused analysis of large-scale drug sensitivity screens, we identify inhibition of the kinase Aurora A as a penetrant synthetic lethal interaction with E-cadherin loss. Combining isogenic cell models, quantitative proteomics, live-cell imaging, patient-derived tumor organoids, and orthotopic xenografts from patients with heavily pre-treated metastatic ILC (mILC), we show that E-cadherin loss alters catenin/Rho/ROCK signaling and imposes a partial defect in centrosomal Aurora A. This defect is normally tolerated but, when exacerbated by pharmacological Aurora A inhibition, causes metaphase arrest and mitotic cell death. Restoring centrosomal Aurora A, or inhibiting ROCK, abolishes this effect. Low tumoral Aurora A is present in most primary lobular tumors. These findings refine the view that high Aurora A expression predicts inhibitor sensitivity and provide the preclinical rationale for trials in mILC.
